holidays.name: National Pick Blueberries Day
holidays.description: A day for heading out to the patch, filling a bucket with plump blueberries, and eating nearly as many as you pick. Peak blueberry season in much of the Northern Hemisphere makes mid-July ideal for it.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food-and-farm observance that grew out of the berry-growing season and the popularity of pick-your-own farms. It has no single known founder.
holidays.funFact: Blueberries are one of the few fruits native to North America, and wild blueberries were gathered by Indigenous peoples for centuries before commercial farming began.

holidays.name: Be a Dork Day
holidays.description: A day to let your inner nerd out with no shame. Wear the goofy outfit, tell the terrible pun, and do the happy dance in public.
holidays.origin: This is a lighthearted unofficial observance that encourages people to embrace their quirks and stop worrying about looking cool. Its exact creator is unclear.
holidays.funFact: The word 'dork' appeared in American slang in the 1960s, and some people think it began as a variation of 'dick,' which is why it was once considered a bit rude.

holidays.name: National Give Something Away Day
holidays.description: A day to clear out your closets and share your stuff with others. Donate, gift, or pass along something you no longer need.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance meant to encourage generosity and decluttering. It has no confirmed origin.
holidays.funFact: Some cultures practice a tradition similar to this: among the Kwakwaka'wakw people, the potlatch ceremony centers on gift-giving to demonstrate status and generosity.

holidays.name: Respect Canada Day
holidays.description: A day that invites Canadians and others to celebrate Canada's culture, politeness, and landscapes. It features maple-flavored everything, hockey talk, and many apologies.
holidays.origin: This observance is attributed to a Canadian-themed awareness day that sprang up as a lighthearted way to appreciate the country, usually in the summer months.
holidays.funFact: Canada has more lakes than the rest of the world's countries combined, with an estimated 2 million of them.

holidays.name: Cow Appreciation Day
holidays.description: A day to thank cows for the milk, cheese, ice cream, and general mooing they bring into our lives. Some fast food restaurants even offer deals if you show up dressed as a cow.
holidays.origin: The most popular version of this was started by a fast food chain as a marketing promotion, and it spread to become a widely recognized fun day in July.
holidays.funFact: A cow can have a best friend and may get stressed when it's separated from it, and cows have been shown to have noticeably lower heart rates when they are with their preferred companions.
